entities.name: ClpX ATPase
observations: The 439-residue query is an exact full-length sequence match to reviewed UniProt entry B4S620 from Prosthecochloris aestuarii.
ClpX is the ATP-dependent specificity component of the Clp protease and can act as an ATP-dependent protein-folding chaperone without ClpP.
The protein forms a hexameric ring and associates with ClpP protease complexes.
Sequence-derived properties: molecular weight 48,292.752 Da, theoretical pI 5.261, GRAVY -0.2123, predicted charge at pH 7 approximately -9.21.
The N-terminal region contains a ClpX-type zinc-binding domain with four conserved cysteine residues; curated reference features assign zinc binding.
The central AAA+ ATPase region contains the conserved P-loop-like ATP-binding motif represented by residues around 139–146 in the reference.
No explicit catalytic reaction equation was retrieved; ATP hydrolysis and chaperone activity are curated functional annotations.
The sequence contains no evident long hydrophobic segment in the reported analysis, consistent with a soluble cytosolic ATPase; localization was not directly curated in the returned evidence.
